content.thinking:
The "monthly-spend-feature" flag toggle at 2026-09-22T14:58:50Z lines up almost exactly with the alert's oldest affected purchase timestamp of 2026-09-22T15:00:00Z, seven days before the alert fired—this is a strong causal match.

The io-summary-cache dependency is described as "optional by design - the page is correct without it," meaning stale cache data shouldn't cause wrong totals, pointing suspicion back toward the flag toggle likely introducing buggy computation logic for spend totals, matching the classic feature-flag-toggle failure mode where a flag switch degrades the service while code and config remain unchanged.

But the reconciliation alert is about stored totals already written incorrectly - that's the hallmark of silent-data-corruption, not feature-flag-toggle, since reverting the flag wouldn't repair the already-corrupted records. The distinction hinges on dating from the oldest wrong record rather than the alert time, and here that oldest bad purchase timestamp lines up almost exactly with when the "monthly-spend-feature" flag toggled, confirming the flag as the trigger for silent-data-corruption rather than a standalone feature-flag-toggle event.

No deployment occurred, only the flag toggle, so bad-deployment and config-induced-failure don't apply here. The dependency check rules out cache staleness since the service works correctly without it, and the pricing dependency shows no signs of failure given flat metrics — I'm now confident this is silent-data-corruption caused by the flag toggle.

hypotheses.subject: monthly-spend-feature
hypotheses.summary: The monthly-spend-feature flag was switched on at 2026-09-22T14:58:50Z, matching almost exactly the oldest purchase the reconciliation check found wrong (2026-09-22T15:00:00Z). The flag enabled a new spend-total computation path that began writing incorrect totals while the service itself stayed fast and error-free - the per-minute metrics show no departure anywhere in the surrounding window, consistent with data corruption that leaves no operational trace until a periodic integrity check catches it. Putting the flag back will stop further drift but will not repair the totals already written for the intervening week.

supporting_evidence.claim: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
the oldest affected purchase was recorded at 2026-09-22T15:00:00Z
240 of 240 shopper totals do not reconcile with the purchases behind them. The widest is short by 1,297.31
no series departs from its baseline anywhere in the window below
monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations (steady state, no error correlation, throughout the log window)

hypotheses.summary: If the corrupted totals turn out not to trace to the feature flag's own logic, the io-summary-cache that io-shop depends on (owned by the same organisation, checkout-platform) is the next candidate, since it exists specifically to hold a shopper's spend figure - though the register notes the page is correct without it, which argues against this being the actual cause.

supporting_evidence.claim: io-summary-cache: internal, owned by checkout-platform ... Holds a shopper's spend figure so the account page does not have to walk their purchase history. Optional by design - the page is correct without it

hypotheses.summary: No cause found beyond the flag toggle coincidence: metrics are flat across the entire retrievable window, there were no deployments in the lookback, and the account-page ClientDisconnected errors visible in the logs are ordinary background noise (~0.5-2.5%) uncorrelated with the reconciliation failure. If the flag toggle is ruled out, nothing else in the evidence names a cause.
